correctness.rationale: For a rooted forest, Möbius inversion gives \(Df(v)=f(v)-f(p(v))\) at every nonroot. Thus Möbius convexity forces \(D^2f(v)\ge0\) away from roots. Hockey-stick domination gives nonnegative coefficients \(h_x=\langle\nu-\mu,\Phi_x\rangle\), and equality of first moments gives the sum of root coefficients equal to zero, hence each root coefficient vanishes. The converse follows by testing hockey-stick functions and both signs of the first power function. For indicators, \(Df\in\{-1,0,1\}\) and therefore \(\lVert D^2f\rVert_\infty\le2\), proving the TV bound. The three-chain example gives equality. Direct zeta/Möbius matrix replay checked the local identities on branching forests.

value.rationale: Rooted trees are explicitly highlighted by the motivating paper, so extending the chain characterization to all rooted forests closes a natural structural gap rather than an arbitrary slice. The same unique-parent lemma gives a sharp dimension-free total-variation comparison, replacing a very coarse general size-dependent bound on this class.
